Special educational needs in England

Published 20 June 2024

Last updated 20 June 2024

Release type: National statistics

Theme: Pupils and schools
Topic: Special educational needs (SEN)

This release presents data from the school census on pupils with special educational needs (SEN) in state-funded schools in England.

Summary

1,644,180 pupils had SEN in state-funded schools in England in January 2024, an increase from 1,607,995 in January 2023.

576,477 pupils had an education, health and care (EHC) plan in January 2024, an increase from 517,268 in January 2023.

1,067,703 pupils received SEN support in January 2024, an increase from 1,090,727 in January 2023.

17.9% of pupils in state-funded schools had SEN in January 2024, up from 17.5% in January 2023.

4.3% of pupils had an EHC plan in January 2024 up from 3.9% in January 2023.

These figures represent pupils with SEN in England in state-funded schools only.

Key findings

The total number of pupils with SEN increased by 36,185 from January 2023 to January 2024.

The number of pupils with an EHC plan increased by 59,209 from January 2023 to January 2024.

The number of pupils receiving SEN support decreased by 23,024 from January 2023 to January 2024.

Among pupils with a primary type of need, the most common type in January 2024 was speech, language and communications needs (SLCN) at 25.6% for EHC plans and 24.7% for SEN support.

Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) was the most common primary type of need in January 2024 for pupils with EHC plans among secondary school pupils.

For pupils with SEN support, the most common type of need for secondary school pupils was social, emotional, and mental health (SEMH) needs.

17.7% of pupils with SEN are taught in special schools in January 2024.

Data and files

Underlying data

All data used in this release are available as open data for download.

Download all data (zip)

Release contents

Section 1: Pupils with SEN
Section 2: Pupils with EHC plans
Section 3: Pupils receiving SEN support
Section 4: Type of need
Section 5: Characteristics of pupils with SEN
Section 6: School type
Section 7: Local authority tables

Methodology

Special educational needs in England: Methodology

About these statistics

About the data

Coverage

This publication covers pupils in state-funded schools in England. It does not cover independent schools, pupil referral units, non-maintained special schools, general hospital schools, and academies where funding is not state-provided. 

For EHC plans only, pupils in early years settings, further education, and post 16 settings, are also included. 

Home educated children with EHC plans are also included.

Due to the data source, this publication is England only.

Data collection

This publication uses data from the school census, which is a statutory collection of all pupils in state-funded schools in England.

The school census is carried out in January, May, and October each year.

Timeliness

This publication is based on data from the January 2024 school census.

Data for January 2025 will be published in Summer 2025.

Contact us

If you have any questions about this publication, contact the SEN team.

Based on my research, the **January 2026** SEND statistics for the UK do not yet exist as published data. The school census data is collected in January each year and published the following summer. As of the most recent available data:

- **January 2024**: 1,644,180 pupils had SEN in state-funded schools in England
- Data for January 2025 was expected to be published in Summer 2025, and January 2026 data would not be collected or published until well into 2026.

Since the question asks about January 2026, this data does not yet exist in any published form.

FINAL: The January 2026 SEND statistics for the UK have not been published yet (data is collected in January and released in Summer of that year; the most recent available figure is 1,644,180 pupils with SEN in England as of January 2024).
